mem.10:
- 2023-01-16–2023-01-22: Jolene completed a demanding electrical engineering project. Deborah visited her late mother’s former home, full of memories; her mother had died a few years earlier. Deborah sits on her mother’s favorite bench by the window to feel connected. Jolene’s mother died in 2022; Jolene remembers her room’s bench and window.
- In 2010, Jolene’s mother gave her a heart-shaped pendant with a bird in Paris. It symbolizes freedom and encourages her to pursue goals. Deborah also keeps a pendant/amulet in memory of her mother.
- Deborah teaches yoga to help people find peace, joy, balance, and connection with themselves. Yoga helped her through a difficult time; teaching brings her happiness and community. She teaches mornings, spends evenings with loved ones, and practices yoga and meditation. Her late mother enjoyed reading at a favorite spot in the house and traveling.
- 2023-01-26: Deborah received a thank-you letter from her yoga group. 2023-01-25 her father died suddenly; she told Jolene on 2023-01-27 the family was shell-shocked. She coped by spending time with family, cherishing memories, and living fully; looking through a family album brought peace. Her parents married in 1993. Deborah and her husband emulate their loving, open relationship and stay close by being there for each other.
- Jolene has snakes Susie and Seraphim, which calm and cheer her. Seraphim once escaped and curled beside her while she gamed. Jolene taught herself games as a child. She and her partner enjoy gaming: played Detroit on console around 2023-01-20–26, planned The Walking Dead for 2023-01-28, and another console game for 2023-02-01.
- 2023-01-31: Deborah met neighbor Anna at yoga in the park; discussed yoga and community. 2023-02-03 they did yoga together, including dance poses and Warrior II (strength/focus), supporting one another. Deborah described a seated chair twist: sit at chair edge, feet planted, twist with hand on knee, hold a few breaths, switch sides; stretches back/shoulders and relieves tension.
- 2023-02-01: Jolene’s engineering professor assigned a large robotics project. She was excited and nervous, enjoyed designing/programming and puzzle-solving. A mini-retreat that day gave her a new outlook and confidence; she exceeded expectations and found exciting project solutions. Interested in green technology for disadvantaged communities, she proposed volunteering to teach STEM to underprivileged children via schools/centers and guest engineers. By 2023-02-09 she had not contacted organizations, wanting to firm up the plan. On 2023-02-09 she shared a planner photo with notebook, pen, notes.
- Around 2023-01-21 Jolene read Neal Stephenson’s “Avalanche” in one sitting; interested in “Sapiens,” about human history and technology’s effects. A story of overcoming adversity reinforced her belief in hard work and possibility.
- Week before 2023-02-04: Jolene planned, researched, designed, and built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community. Challenging and rewarding; seeing it provide clean water felt surreal, satisfying, and purposeful. Hopes to keep creating sustainable solutions. On 2023-02-04 she said she was on an emotional rollercoaster but coping.
- Deborah encourages Jolene to breathe, remember her purpose and strengths, stay in touch, and care for herself. Jolene appreciates this and promised to stay in touch.
- Deborah finds calm on a forest trail in a park and at a nearby beach. She visited Bali in 2022, calling it gorgeous and peaceful; waves and fresh air made beach yoga wonderful. Jolene wanted to try beach yoga (2023-02-22). Jolene’s summer-2022 vacation photo showed a calming beach sunset over water in Bogotá. Deborah reflects at a waterside spot near her mother’s former home; nature and her mother’s amulet comfort her. Anna wears a pendant for her mother; sharing memories/keepsakes brought them closer. Deborah likes birdsong and breezes.
- A friend gave Deborah flowers while she was struggling; they brought hope, courage, warmth, and appreciation. 2023-02-22: Deborah visited a garden with flowers in buckets; roses and dahlias comfort her. She had recently lost a friend; memories reminded her life is special. Her photo with Karlie from a hike the previous summer was their last photo together and makes Deborah smile.
- 2023-02-21: Jolene had dinner and drinks with friends and enjoyed relaxing.
- 2023-02-25: Jolene balances engineering school, gaming with her partner, yoga, and meditation. Yoga helps her relax, gain perspective, and feel alert/motivated. When overwhelmed she pauses to breathe/meditate for calm and clarity. She and her partner sometimes do yoga together, which relaxes them and strengthens their bond. They met in a college engineering class, became friends then partners; together three years as of 2023-02-25, unmarried and taking things slowly. A ring visible on partner’s hand in a photo was decorative, not a wedding ring. They enjoy engineering projects together and understand each other’s challenges.
- 2023-02-24: Deborah jogged in a nearby park for the first time and planned morning jogs as a routine; exercise connects her to her body. 2023-02-25 she shared a photo of someone on a bench watching sunset, a reminder to find peace amid chaos. 2023-02-24 Jolene did yoga/meditation for self-care; Deborah also practiced to reset.
- 2023-02-26: Jolene took Seraphim to the park; it enjoyed exploring. People are surprised to see a tame snake. An accompanying photo showed a lizard among leaves.
- 2023-03-02: Anna had recently made Deborah tasty vegan tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry with ginger and soy sauce. Jolene likes lasagna. Jolene felt overwhelmed by exams, deadlines, and tasks and wanted to prioritize mental health. Deborah advised small study goals, a planner/scheduler, and self-care, and offered help with a study plan. Deborah offered her a mug like a photo’s yellow cup with handwritten message; Jolene said it cheered her.
- 2023-03-10: Deborah hosted a yoga class for interested neighbors; they enjoyed it (photo of women posing together). On 2023-03-13 she said she liked sharing exercise and seeing its benefits.
- 2023-03-13: Jolene struggled to manage engineering assignments and asked to discuss time management. They agreed to find a time; Jolene would check her schedule and get back to Deborah. No time was set.
- 2023-03-22, 5:35 pm: Deborah checked in about Jolene’s exams/deadlines. Jolene said keeping up with everything felt stressful. She uses Pomodoro (25 minutes work, 5-minute break) but struggles to prioritize. Deborah uses daily schedules/to-do lists and shared a photo of her notepad list. Jolene shared a photo of her notes on a counter from the prior Friday; large task lists overwhelm her and she often doesn’t know where to start. Deborah introduced the Eisenhower Matrix, sorting tasks into four categories by urgency and importance, and shared a photo of scissors on paper illustrating it. Jolene found the visualization helpful and agreed to try the method.
- Also 2023-03-22: Deborah reminded Jolene to look after herself and shared that she and Anna had watched a sunset by the sea, realizing they inspire one another. Photo showed someone walking on a beach with a surfboard. Jolene said it made her think about learning to surf, but she needed spare time. She had gathered information, watched videos, and bought a beginner’s guide; still needed to find the right time/place for a lesson. Deborah encouraged her to pursue it step by step and enjoy the experience, sharing a photo of surfboards leaning against a palm tree. Jolene felt encouraged and said she would keep pushing to make surfing happen.
mem.20:
Jolene and Deborah are friends who discuss family, yoga, work, grief, self-care, hobbies, and shared memories.

**Deborah:** Her mother died before 2023; her father died suddenly on 2023-01-25. Her parents married in 1993 and were loving, open, and supportive. Family photos and time together helped Deborah cope after her father’s death. Her mother loved reading and travel, and sitting by windows—on a special bench in the morning and reading in the evenings. Deborah visits her mother’s old house, does yoga there, and sits by the window to feel close to her. She also visits a nearby waterside spot with her mother’s amulet and wears a keepsake pendant.

Deborah teaches yoga because it helped her through a difficult period; she values its calm and community. Her group sent an appreciative letter on 2023-01-26. She met neighbor Anna at park yoga on 2023-01-31; they bonded over yoga and keepsake pendants for their late mothers. Warrior II builds strength and focus; Deborah described a chair-supported seated twist for back and shoulders. She hosted neighbors’ yoga on 2023-03-10 and started a neighborhood class by 2023-03-13. She likes candles, essential oils, mellow instrumental music (especially “Savana”), and the album “Sleep.” Gentle breathing/grounding flow helps in hard times. She learned mindfulness through workshops and books, made a retreat meditation guide on 2023-08-12, and led meditation-yoga for elderly people at a care home during the week of 2023-08-07. On 2023-08-18 she said she had told Anna her life story on 2023-08-11; Anna was kind and Deborah valued their connection.

She loves a park near home with forest trail and beach, where she does yoga and reflects. A special bench there was where she and her mother talked about dreams and life; they once watched a beautiful sunset in silence. Returning brings peace, gratitude, and thankfulness for their time together. Deborah likes roses and dahlias; after friend Karlie died shortly before 2023-02-22, a garden and their last photo together (from a hike the prior summer) comforted her. Art shows evoke her late mother and can be comforting and difficult. She jogged in a nearby park on 2023-02-24 and planned regular morning runs; she and Anna had a running group by 2023-07-09. She dislikes dogs, has cats, and said she takes them running morning and evening. She organizes mindfulness/self-care events and began community cleanup/fundraising by 2023-08-01. In July 2023 she organized a yoga event with local businesses/venues, yoga, food stalls, and live music.

Deborah used to play video games; she and her husband took turns and enjoyed detective games, which helped them bond. They also enjoyed outdoor nature outings.

On 2023-08-21, Deborah recalled visiting a meaningful place and sitting on a bench where she and her mother used to talk. She felt nostalgia and longing, but also gratitude. She brought flowers; her mother loved flowers and simple pleasures. Her mother taught her to slow down, see beauty, and find joy. Deborah enjoys walks, mindfulness, yoga, meditation, and taking photos on walks; a sunset over water is especially cherished. Walks feel like a “reboot” to her.

**Jolene:** Engineering student/engineer who wants to create sustainable solutions for communities in need. Finished a demanding electrical-engineering project during 2023-01-16–22. Her mother died in 2022; memories include her room, bench, and window. In Paris in 2010 her mother gave her a heart-shaped bird pendant symbolizing freedom and pursuit of goals. On 2023-02-01 Jolene was excited/nervous about a robotics assignment; a mini-retreat helped her find solutions. The week before 2023-02-04 she designed and built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community; seeing it work felt meaningful. She wants to explore green tech in disadvantaged areas and proposed STEM volunteering for underprivileged children; as of 2023-02-09 she had not contacted partners. She had an engineering breakthrough on 2023-03-24; completed a solar-powered vehicle in May 2023. By 2023-06-06 she was interning at a well-known engineering firm, applying school learning to real projects; work-life balance was hard. A photo showed construction-worker colleagues. She did yoga atop Mount Talkeetna on 2023-06-05. She had practiced yoga/meditation sporadically for about three years. On 2023-08-12 she was working on an affordable, productive aerial-surveillance prototype for emergency response/environmental monitoring.

Jolene has snakes Susie and female Seraphim. Susie, adopted around August 2021 when Jolene felt lonely, helps her stay strong and notice small joys; snakes calm her and teach patience. Seraphim was acquired in 2022, once escaped and was found snuggled under the bed, and once curled beside Jolene while gaming. Jolene took Seraphim to a park on 2023-02-26 (related photo showed a lizard among leaves) and bought her a new aquarium on 2023-06-24.

Jolene and her partner met in a college engineering class; friends before dating, together three years as of 2023-02-25, unmarried and taking it slowly. A ring in a photo was decoration, not a wedding ring. They enjoy games and engineering projects; games mentioned include Detroit, It Takes Two, and planned The Walking Dead (2023-01-28). Gaming helps them bond. Jolene taught herself games as a child. She likes lasagna; read Neal Stephenson’s “Avalanche” in one sitting around 2023-01-21, likes “Sapiens,” and was inspired by a story of success through hardship. A photo from a 2022 summer vacation in Bogotá showed a calming beach sunset.

On 2023-08-17 Jolene bought her partner an Xbox console as a gift; photo showed black Xbox and Yoda figure, and he enjoyed playing it. On 2023-08-19 she recommended Zelda: Breath of the Wild (Switch) and Animal Crossing: New Horizons; she and her partner play Overcooked 2 for bets, and she once won three large pizzas. A photo showed a man and woman sitting before a computer. On 2023-08-21 she said they had received Battlefield 1 for the console the previous week. She asked Deborah about balancing studies/hobbies and planned a schedule after Deborah advised prioritizing and allocating set times.

Jolene has faced study/deadline overwhelm (2023-03-02); uses breathing, meditation, yoga, sometimes Pomodoro (25 minutes work/5-minute break). Deborah recommended small goals, a planner, and Eisenhower Matrix; Jolene found it helpful. Yoga helps Jolene relax, gain perspective, alertness, and motivation; partner sometimes joins. She likes lavender/rosemary and music by Nils Frahm and Ólafur Arnalds. After losing project files in a crash (2023-08-01), Susie, games, yoga, and meditation helped; meditation restored calm/clarity (2023-08-12). She designs space/engineering-themed notebooks; uses a bullet journal and time management by 2023-08-16. Interested in mindfulness but hadn’t tried it.

Jolene wants to learn surfing; by 2023-03-22 she had watched videos and got a beginner guide but needed time/place. Deborah encouraged her; they planned a visit to Jolene’s peaceful tree-ringed lake together (2023-07-09). Deborah encourages Jolene to stay in touch and care for herself.

On 2023-08-21 Jolene said she was trying to do more yoga and meditation to relax and focus, and called savasana (corpse pose) her favorite restful pose because it helps her let go and surrender. She had practiced yoga for three years, using it to escape study/work stress, and said she was finding her zen again. She shared a photo of a green cushion on the floor before a window and a humorous photo of someone lying on the floor with a paper bag. Deborah encouraged her.
